label: Colon cancer

approval.note: Draft checklist from the NCG Management of Colorectal Cancer flow (colon): needs a clinician's check

site_note: V2 item 5.3 (two primaries): only on a Case File linked to the same patient's other Case File, and only for histopathology, cytology, IHC and molecular records: among several candidates for one record, or several documents carrying a required value, one that names another protocol's site and not this one steps aside and is named on the row for review; a document naming no site never does, and when every candidate names another site every candidate stays. Organ words only. A preference, never a filter; a patient with one cancer is checked as before. The rectal checklist shares the colorectal words (colon, colorectal, sigmoid, bowel, intestin), so a report that names both sites does not step aside; the preference only applies between two linked primaries.
note: Draft checklist from the NCG Management of Colorectal Cancer flow, colon (pages 2 to 4): needs a clinician's check. Colon only: rectal cancer has its own checklist. This NCG file prints no Essential / Optimal / Optional letters, so every tier is a proposal (an item in the page 2 Workup list is proposed Essential; items NCG calls optional, 'not routinely' or 'may be' are proposed Optional), to be confirmed by the hospital Tumour Board (clinical review before real use). The MMR and RAS / BRAF tiers differ from the rectal checklist on purpose. The system records the stage as written and never computes it; no treatment advice. India first: the National Cancer Grid guideline is the only source, and its page 2 footnote allows a chest X-ray in place of CT chest.
settings_note: The setting of the Case File, chosen by the clinician from what the signed reports record (the system never computes a stage and never decides the setting). Each record carries its tier per setting; until a setting is recorded the strictest tier applies. Draft checklist: needs a clinician's check.

core_data_source: NHS England, Streamlining MDT meetings (2020), p.11 'minimum core data requirements'; aligned with the NCG Virtual Tumour Board case template (India)

post_board.record_fields_source: EUSOMA 2020 (names of all participants, evidence on decisions); Victorian Cancer MDM quality framework 2018 (report errors/changes raised, divergent recommendations and dissenting clinicians); PM-JAY HBP 2.2 s.3.9 (tumour board decision and treatment plan)

policy_basis: PM-JAY Health Benefit Package 2.2 user guidelines (NHA, 2021), section 3.9: pre-authorization is mandatory at each step of cancer care and the decision on appropriate care is to be taken by a multidisciplinary tumour board; NHS England MDT streamlining guidance (2020) pre-listing conditions. The NCG book itself asks for the board: "(DISCUSS IN MULTIDISCIPLINARY MEETING," (NCG Management of Colorectal Cancer (colon flow), page 2); the Tumour Board Case File is that discussion, so no separate record is required for it (orchestrator, night-v3 Phase 2).
